alignments.note: Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English (rule 20).
Finite verb; the subject pronoun is written separately in the Hebrew, so the verb keeps only the lexical verb.
Definite direct-object marker; the ASV writes the object bare, spending no word on the object relation (rule 16).
Construct noun. The phrase's single *the* stands on the attributive's own article (s007), which is a present article morpheme, so `שַׁעַר` keeps only its own word (rule 47).

Article on the attributive adjective takes the phrase's one written *the*; the head noun is a construct that can carry no article of its own, and a present article morpheme takes the English before a supplied one (rule 47).
Nomen rectum of `שַׁעַר` taking the relational *of* (rule 19), and itself a construct with no article morpheme, so the second *the* is supplied to it (rule 29).
Construct noun; the chain's rectum carries an article, which takes the single written *the*, so `חוֹמָה` keeps only its own word (rule 29).
Article segmented off the toponym takes the phrase's one *the*, exactly as `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* does (rule 29); it is not set aside as lexicalized in the name.
Nomen rectum with the relational *of* (rule 19), rendered anarthrously.
Finite verb with its English subject pronoun (rule 17).

`לָרֹב` is rendered by the single English word *much*, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the preposition shares the noun's unit, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme. Marking the `לְ` `unrepresented` beside a bare `רֹב` → *much* was available, but no English word here is spent on the preposition in particular.

review_notes: Both articles in this verse sit on words the ASV renders after a fronted *the*: s007 on the attributive of a construct head, s012 on a toponym. Rule 47 and rule 29's toponym rider give each the written *the* and leave the construct nouns bare.
The object marker is unrepresented; *built the upper gate* spends no word on the object relation.
